newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Top Colombian daily urges Samper to resign.
newsitem.headline: Top Colombian daily urges Samper to resign.

text.p: A leading daily urged President Ernesto Samper to resign for the good of his country on Thursday after likening his government to "an unburied corpse" and saying Colombia was "on the brink of an abyss."
"Colombians are more convinced every day that the only patriotic solution the president has is to resign along with his cabinet," Bogota's El Espectador newspaper said.

"Social discontent is growing and on its way toward erupting in a massive explosion that will leave no stone unturned," it added in an editorial, referring to growing unemployment and widespread criticism of recently announced economic belt-tightening measures.

The measures, including a government's plan to hold public sector workers to an 13.5 percent wage hike this year despite inflation of more than 21 percent in 1996, led unions to set a Feb. 11 deadline for a nationwide strike last week.

El Espectador, one of Colombia's most respected dailies, urged Samper to step down several times last year during the political crisis over charges that he received millions of dollars in drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.

Thursday's editorial made no direct reference to those charges, which severely weakened Samper's government. But it cited a general breakdown in law and order highlighted by seemingly uncontrolled levels of violence and leftist guerrilla attacks in the countryside as among the reasons Samper should leave office.
"The country is on the brink of an abyss. It is walking toward ruin with closed eyes," the newspaper said.

"(The government) has a bomb in its hands that could explode at any minute. The fuse is burning but it has done nothing but cover its ears," it added. "Colombians are faced with the breakdown of political institutions and the definitive onslaught of chaos."

Samper's term of office ends in August 1998. But El Espectador, which said he had offered his countrymen nothing but "false illusions, lies and a lack of seriousness," said his government was like an "unburied corpse" for which a death certificate should have been issued long ago.
